origin: The core is accurate and on the fact sheet: a Chinese barge is suspected of damaging the cable during a salvage job, the coast guard boarded it and questioned the captain, the 2023 cuts and the Hong Tai 58 conviction happened as described. The last two sentences assert deliberate state sabotage and a cover story as fact, while the fact sheet shows only a suspicion, an investigation just opened, and a recent precedent of a Chinese captain's cable damage being ruled negligent. Expected honest rating: 40 to 60.

evidence_down.evidence_note: Real. Focus Taiwan/CNA, "Chinese barge captain not prosecuted over Dongyin subsea cable damage", published 2026-07-15, https://focustaiwan.tw/society/202607150019 (src/ft-2026-07-15-no-prosecution.md). Chinese original with more detail, CNA, 2026-07-15, https://www.cna.com.tw/news/aloc/202607150306.aspx (src/cna-2026-07-15-no-prosecution.md). Verified: date, office, "insufficient evidence", the fragment of the stranded vessel, the survey dropped over national security concerns and approved, confirmation of the anchoring position with Chunghwa Telecom staff, "followed approved instructions", "difficult to conclude that he had acted negligently or intentionally damaged the cable". Also reported by Taipei Times, 2026-07-16 (not fetched).
pushes: New information that adds to the fact sheet: on July 15, 2026, Taiwan's Lienchiang District Prosecutors Office announced that it will not prosecute the Hai Hong Gong 66's captain, citing insufficient evidence. Prosecutors said a fragment of the stranded fishing vessel struck and damaged the cable while the wreck was being broken up for removal. The owner's salvage plan had dropped a preliminary underwater survey because of national security concerns, and Taiwanese authorities approved that revised plan, so no one at the scene knew the cable lay directly beneath the wreck. Based on Chunghwa Telecom employees' testimony and messages on the captain's phone, prosecutors found he confirmed his anchoring position with Chunghwa Telecom staff before dropping anchor and tried to avoid the cable area, and that he followed the approved salvage instructions, making it difficult to conclude he acted negligently or intentionally.
